D010-D006_h001.question:
I drive for a courier company, so my days are usually long, but for about two months recently I was like a motor that wouldn’t shut off. I barely slept and still felt wired, pacing, taking extra routes just to keep moving. I’d go from feeling on top of the world to snapping at coworkers or customers over nothing in the same hour. I couldn’t stop talking, even when people looked uncomfortable—I’d ramble, jump from topic to topic, and silence felt unbearable. My sex drive went through the roof; I was messaging multiple women, including exes, and pushing for hookups constantly. I even tried to start this “side logistics company,” threw a bunch of my savings into some sketchy app and trucks I hadn’t really researched.

During that time I was sure my ex was cheating on me, checking her socials nonstop, convinced every comment was proof, even though we weren’t together. I also saw people in the back of my van or on the street who disappeared when I looked twice.

Then I crashed. For about five months I’ve mostly felt flat and low, like nothing is enjoyable anymore—not friends, games, sex, anything. Getting dressed or choosing what to eat can paralyze me. I’m messing up routes and sometimes can’t even leave my bed. But even in these really down weeks, when I’m not amped up at all, I still sometimes see figures in my apartment or in my mirrors and get stuck on the idea that my ex is secretly with someone else, even though I know it doesn’t make sense.
D010-D006_h001.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Adjustment Disorder

D010-D006_h002.question:
I’m a computational biologist, so I’m used to tracking timelines, and this whole thing feels like a really messy dataset.

About seven months ago I started feeling “amped up” and on edge. For roughly two months straight I was constantly wired and irritable. The tiniest things my husband did—like chewing too loud—would make me snap. I barely slept but didn’t feel tired, just charged. I couldn’t sit still at my desk; I’d pace in the lab, start multiple analyses at once, and talk nonstop in meetings, cutting people off because my thoughts felt too fast to keep inside. I suddenly wanted to network with everyone—Slack messages, late-night Zooms, even reaching out to people I barely knew. I also put a chunk of our savings into some sketchy biotech startups after skimming a few abstracts, convinced I’d found “the next big thing,” and now I really regret it.

During that high-energy stretch, and even afterward, I became convinced something was wrong with my organs—like my liver was rotting or my blood was contaminated—despite normal tests. Sometimes I’d randomly taste metal or chemicals in my mouth when I wasn’t eating.

After the energized phase burned out, I crashed into about five months of feeling deeply low. I lost interest in friends and stopped replying in group chats. Outside of work, I mostly stayed in bed. My thinking felt slow and foggy, like trying to code through molasses; even reading papers was hard. I’m still having those strange tastes and worries about my body, even in weeks when my mood is more flat than high or low, and it’s really messing with both my work and my marriage.
D010-D006_h002.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Adjustment Disorder

D010-D006_h003.question:
I’m a foreman, so I’m used to stress, but this past year has been different.  

About seven months ago I started feeling revved up and pissed off all the time. The smallest thing on site would set me off—guys stacking lumber wrong, a late delivery—and I’d be screaming, throwing tools. I couldn’t sit still; I was pacing the scaffolding, walking the site back and forth for no reason. I’d talk so fast my crew and even my wife would ask me to slow down, but I just couldn’t. I was driving way over the speed limit, cutting people off, thinking I was invincible. That kind of “on edge and wired” feeling has gone on for a couple of months straight and really messed up work and home.  

On top of that, I’m convinced something’s wrong under my skin, like bugs or wires moving around, and I feel them crawling even when nothing’s there. Those sensations and beliefs have kept going even when my mood crashed. For the last five months I’ve been crying at random, nothing feels good anymore—not my kids, not fishing—and my head feels full of fog, like I can’t think straight. Even then, the feeling of things crawling and this certainty my body’s messed up never goes away.
D010-D006_h003.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Adjustment Disorder

D010-D006_h004.question:
I work in investments, so I’m used to stress and long hours, but this has been…different.  

About seven months ago I started feeling “on top of the world.” For around two months I barely slept and still had tons of energy. I was taking on way too many deals at once, calling clients at odd hours, talking so fast in meetings my team couldn’t keep up. I was snapping from being overly cheerful to suddenly furious if anyone questioned me. I was driving way too fast between meetings, blowing money on impulsive things, even using cocaine a few times. My sex drive shot through the roof; I was pushing my wife for sex constantly and messaging old flings.  

During that time, and even after my mood calmed down, I became convinced my wife was cheating. I check her phone, track her location. I also get these weird bitter-metallic tastes in my mouth out of nowhere, like I’m being poisoned. That’s been happening for weeks even when my mood is just flat or low.  

For the last five months I’ve mostly felt empty, mentally foggy, pulling away from friends and family, barely functioning at work, but the cheating idea and those strange tastes haven’t gone away.
D010-D006_h004.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Adjustment Disorder

D010-D006_h005.question:
For about seven months now I’ve felt like I’ve been living in two completely different gears.

The first stretch, maybe two months, I was on fire. I barely slept, maybe three hours a night, but I didn’t feel tired. I’d be pacing the house, hopping between emails, new product ideas, reorganizing the whole company structure at 3 a.m. I couldn’t sit still in meetings; I’d talk nonstop, cutting people off, jumping from one idea to the next. I felt on top of the world, like everything was clicking. I also got very sexually driven—porn constantly, flirting with employees, and I actually hooked up with a junior staffer on a business trip, which is completely unlike me and has really damaged my marriage and the company.

During that “high,” I became convinced TV anchors were sending me signals about our business strategy, and sometimes water or coffee would suddenly taste like metal or chemicals, even when others said it was normal.

Then that high just disappeared. For the last five months I’ve felt hollow, like there’s nothing inside. I’ve lost interest in golf, seeing friends, even the business. I can’t focus; I misplace documents, forget appointments. Work has really suffered. But even in this flat, empty state, I still sometimes feel the news is aimed directly at me, and I still get those strange, phantom tastes, even though the “up” mood is completely gone.
D010-D006_h005.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Adjustment Disorder

D010-D006_h006.question:
It started about six months ago. For a solid two months I was on this…tear. I was constantly on edge, snapping at my crew over tiny things, like a cable being out of place. I’d pace around set, couldn’t sit through a single meeting. My mind felt wired, like I’d had twenty coffees, and I was talking nonstop—jumping from one “brilliant” idea to the next so fast no one could keep up. Silence felt unbearable.  

I started driving way too fast between shoots, cutting people off, thinking I was untouchable. I blew a big chunk of my savings on new cameras and a spontaneous trip to scout in a war zone, convinced I was destined to make “the film that changes history.” I really believed I had some sort of special vision, like I’d been chosen for something huge.  

What’s strange is the sensations on my skin—like bugs crawling up my arms or someone brushing my neck when no one’s there. Those and the feeling that I’m this “chosen” director didn’t go away when my mood finally crashed and I wasn’t amped up anymore. Even in those flat, exhausted weeks, the crawling feeling and the conviction about my “special mission” kept hanging around.
D010-D006_h006.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D006_h007.question:
It started about two months ago. At first I just felt amazing, like I could do anything, but then I’d snap and get really short with people over nothing. I’ll be laughing with the kids in my class one minute and then the next I’m furious at a coworker for breathing too loud. It flips so fast I can’t keep up with it.

I can’t sit still. In the classroom I’m pacing, rearranging the room over and over, starting projects at 2 a.m. and never finishing them. My head feels like it’s racing, and I talk nonstop—my friends say they can’t get a word in. Silence feels unbearable, like something bad will happen if I stop talking.

I’ve also done really stupid things—speeding way over the limit at night “just to feel alive,” spending money I don’t have, hooking up with people I barely know. Work’s been a mess; I’ve called in “sick” or left lessons half-prepared.

What really scares me is that, even on the weeks when my mood settles and I’m not wired or irritable, I still feel like the world is about to end. I’m convinced some huge disaster is coming. Sometimes I feel things crawling on my skin or like someone’s brushing my arm when no one’s there. Those sensations and beliefs kept going for a couple of weeks even when my energy and mood were more or less normal.
D010-D006_h007.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D006_h008.question:
It started about four months ago. For the first two months I was “wired” all the time. I was snapping at everyone over nothing—my wife would ask about the corn feed and I’d blow up. I couldn’t sit still; I’d be pacing between the barn and the field at midnight, starting new projects, fixing equipment that didn’t need fixing. My mind was racing so fast my words tumbled out; my family kept telling me to slow down because they couldn’t follow what I was saying. 

During that time I also started doing things that aren’t like me at all—flirting and messing around with women in town, even though I’ve been married for over 30 years. I knew it was reckless but felt driven.

Along with that, I became convinced my wife was cheating. I’d watch her constantly, check her phone, certain she was sneaking around, even though I couldn’t prove anything. I also kept feeling things crawling on my skin at night, like bugs under my clothes, but there was nothing there.

The strange thing is, even after the “high” wore off and my mood calmed for a couple of weeks, I still felt the crawling and still believed she was unfaithful, even though I wasn’t revved up anymore.
D010-D006_h008.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D006_h009.question:
It started around six months ago. At first it was like I’d had three cups of coffee all the time. I was buzzing, couldn’t sit still, pacing the house, reorganizing drawers at 3 a.m., then going out and walking the neighborhood before my census shifts. I was snapping at my husband over little things—him breathing too loud, the TV volume—flying off the handle in a way that’s not like me. I’d talk his ear off, and my daughter’s too, jumping from one idea to the next without letting anyone get a word in.

I also got carried away with online shopping—clothes, gadgets, things for the house we didn’t need. I ran up our credit cards so badly my husband had to take them away. That whole “high” lasted a good two months and really messed up my work; I kept arguing with people at their doors.

But even after I finally calmed down, the strange things didn’t stop. For at least a couple of weeks, maybe longer, I kept having this absolute conviction that one of the supervisors at the census office was secretly in love with me, sending me “messages” through meeting times. And I kept smelling cigarette smoke in the house, strong and sour, when no one smokes and there was nothing burning. Those smells and that belief have come and gone on their own, even when my mood feels more or less normal.
D010-D006_h009.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D006_h010.question:
For the last year or so, I’ve been feeling like I’m coming apart. About four months ago I got into this really “amped up” phase that lasted a good two months. I was constantly on edge and snapping at people over nothing—coworkers, callers, even my sister. It felt like my fuse was gone. I couldn’t sit still at the dispatch console; I was pacing between calls, rearranging things, talking nonstop, even when people were clearly annoyed. I’d pick up extra shifts, drive way over the speed limit home at 3 a.m., and blow money I don’t really have on random stuff, without thinking.

During that same time, and still now, I hear these voices, like a couple of people talking about me through my headset, even when my line is dead. Off shift, I’ll hear them in my apartment, like they’re in the next room commenting on what I’m doing. I’ve also become convinced that certain calls, certain license plates, even songs on the radio are sending me specific messages. 

What really scares me is that even after that revved‑up, irritable “high” finally calmed down a few weeks ago, the voices and the feeling that things are about me never went away.
D010-D006_h010.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D006_h011.question:
It started about three months ago. At first it felt like a “creative high,” but it got scary. For about a month I was constantly on edge and snapping at people over nothing—like if my editor sent a tiny correction, I’d explode. I couldn’t sit still; I’d pace my apartment at 3 a.m., storyboard three chapters at once, jump from one idea to another so fast I couldn’t finish anything. My head felt like ten tabs open, all playing at once. I missed multiple deadlines even though I was working nonstop because I kept starting new panels and tossing them.

Around that same time I started hearing this low male voice, like it was right behind me, commenting on my drawings, telling me the world was about to collapse, that there was no point finishing the series because everything would be wiped out. I became convinced some huge disaster was coming and that everyone else was just pretending not to see it.

What scares me is that even after that “amped up” phase calmed down and my mood felt more flat and drained again for a few weeks, the voice and that conviction the world is ending didn’t go away—they kept going even when I wasn’t feeling revved up or irritable anymore.
D010-D006_h011.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D010-D006_h012.question:
It started about six months ago. For a full month I felt… almost too good. I was buzzing with energy, waking up after three hours of sleep feeling fantastic. I was talking nonstop, calling my children at odd hours with all these “big plans,” rearranging the whole house, starting projects I couldn’t possibly finish—painting, gardening, even trying to write a book all at once. My mind wouldn’t slow down; thoughts were tumbling over each other so fast I could barely keep up. I know I was overwhelming people, and I stopped going to my senior group because I couldn’t sit still long enough.

During that same time, I became convinced the TV and the radio were sending me secret messages—little phrases in the news that were “meant” for me. I also kept hearing a man and a woman talking about me in the next room when no one was there.

What’s strange is that even after I calmed down and my mood went back to normal, those things didn’t stop. For at least a couple of weeks, I wasn’t overly happy or energized anymore, but I still heard the voices and still felt like the programs on TV were directed at me.
D010-D006_h012.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D010-D006_h013.question:
For the past year or so, things have really gone off the rails. About six months ago, I had this stretch, maybe a month long, where I was constantly on edge and snapping at people over nothing—coworkers, my sister, even strangers. I barely slept but didn’t feel tired. I’d pace my apartment at 3 a.m., writing long, rambling emails about audit “insights” that didn’t really make sense when I looked back. D010-D006_h016.question:
For the last seven months I’ve felt like I’ve fallen off a cliff emotionally. Most days I just feel heavy and flat, like there’s no point to anything. I used to love working the floor, talking to guests about wine, hanging with the other sommeliers after shift. Now I avoid everyone, trade shifts when I can, and go straight home to bed. I’m sleeping 12–14 hours, sometimes napping between lunch and dinner service, but I still wake up exhausted. A lot of nights I just lie there thinking it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up, not that I’d actually do anything, more like I wouldn’t mind if it just… stopped.

I’ve had this strong smell of smoke or rotting cork follow me around when there’s nothing there. A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)

D010-D006_h017.question:
It’s been about seven months now that I feel like someone hollowed me out. I sit at my desk and stare at the typewriter; words used to pour out of me, but I don’t care about writing anymore, or reading, or even my evening walks with my wife. D010-D006_h018.question:

Even when I slept 8–9 hours, I’d wake up feeling as if I hadn’t rested at all. D010-D006_h019.question:

I stopped going to yoga with my friends, stopped working on my classroom art projects I used to love. When I did sleep, I kept having these horrible, vivid dreams where my students were hurt and I’d wake up drenched in sweat, heart racing, then lie there dreading the next night. D010-D006_h020.question:

D010-D006_h021.question:

D010-D006_h022.question:
I work in infosec, mostly pentesting, so my job is long stretches of focus. About six months ago I hit this stretch where, for two weeks, I was just…amped and pissed off at the same time. Tiny stuff set me off—someone breathing loud in the office and I’d snap. I was barely sleeping but didn’t feel tired, pacing around, starting three different audits at once, jumping between terminals, unable to stay on one task for more than a minute. My team lead finally sent me home because I was too chaotic and confrontational with clients.

During that time, I became convinced I’d basically “evolved” beyond normal hackers—that I was being watched by agencies because of my “unique” skills. I could feel things crawling under my skin, like little electric currents running along my arms and back, even when nothing was there. Those sensations and the idea I was being monitored actually kept going for a few weeks after the “high” dropped and my mood flattened.

Then I crashed hard. For the last two months I’ve been moving like I’m underwater—walking slow, just staring at the screen, not starting tickets. I stopped answering friends, skipped work, and a few weeks ago I stockpiled my anxiety meds and wrote goodbye emails. I didn’t send them, but it got that far.
D010-D006_h022.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa

D010-D006_h023.question:
It’s been going on for about a year now, in waves. The first big spell was around two weeks where I felt almost… too good. I’m 70, I shouldn’t have that much energy. I was up half the night rearranging the house, calling my children at odd hours with “new ideas,” pacing the hallway. I couldn’t sit through a TV show or even finish a crossword; my mind kept jumping. It felt wonderful at the time, like I was glowing, but I stopped paying bills, missed my blood pressure meds, and my daughter had to step in.

During that time, I became convinced that the cardiologist I saw years ago is secretly in love with me. I still believe he sends me messages through the TV. I also hear voices—one sounds like a man quietly commenting on what I do, another sometimes calls my name. Those voices and the belief about the doctor have stayed, even in the last two months where my mood has crashed.

Lately I can barely get off the couch. I move so slowly it’s embarrassing, and I don’t bother cooking or going to my seniors’ group. I catch myself thinking it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up, though I haven’t made any plans.
D010-D006_h023.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa

D010-D006_h024.question:
It’s been about a year of this back-and-forth, but what pushed me to come in was the last few months.  

About three months ago I went into this “high” phase that lasted around two weeks. At work on the unit I was bouncing between feeling amazing and chatty with everyone to suddenly snapping at coworkers over nothing. I couldn’t sit still—constantly pacing the halls, reorganizing the med cart, starting multiple projects at home and at work, never finishing any of them. I’d be on a care plan, then jump to rewriting a protocol in my head, then cleaning my whole apartment at 3 a.m. My manager had to send me home early a couple of times because I was too wound up to actually focus and it was affecting patient care.

During that time—and since then—I’ve been convinced people are watching me. I feel like the hospital administration and even patients’ families are tracking me through the cameras, talking about me. I hear this man’s voice, like over an intercom in my head, commenting on what I’m doing, sometimes saying they’re “coming for” my license. That’s happened even on days when my mood isn’t up or down, just kind of flat.

Then for the last two months I’ve been mostly low. I stopped going to yoga, don’t really see friends, and when I’m home I pace endlessly or pick at my skin until it bleeds because I can’t relax but also can’t make myself do anything meaningful. On really bad days, when I’m walking over the overpass to the bus, I get these strong urges to just step off, or when a car speeds by I think about stepping into the lane. I haven’t made a plan, but the impulses scare me. I’ve been calling in sick more, and when I do work, I’m slower and distracted, which isn’t safe in my job. The paranoid feeling and the voice haven’t really gone away, even when the mood stuff shifts.
D010-D006_h024.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa

D010-D006_h025.question:
I work as a live sound engineer, so I’m used to long, weird hours, but about six months ago something really changed. For a couple of weeks I felt unbelievably wired and “on top of the world.” I barely slept and was bouncing between projects—re-editing old mixes, starting three new podcasts, rearranging my whole studio at 3 a.m. I couldn’t finish anything because I’d keep jumping to the next “brilliant” idea. My friends and coworkers said I was talking too fast and getting in everyone’s way at gigs. I honestly felt fantastic, like everything and everyone was somehow connected to me.

Around that time and since then, I started noticing odd things. I’ll hear a random comment at a café or see a lyric on a poster and feel like it’s aimed specifically at me, like there’s some hidden message. Sometimes I get this weird metallic or chemical taste in my mouth out of nowhere, even when I’m not eating.

What scares me is that those “messages” and strange tastes kept happening for a couple of weeks even after that high energy phase crashed. For the last two months I’ve been moving in slow motion, struggling to get out of bed, walking slowly, just going through the motions at shows. I don’t really care about how my mixes sound anymore, which is not like me. I catch myself thinking it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up, though I haven’t made any plans to hurt myself.
D010-D006_h025.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
